title: Enterprise Implementation Manager
why: Closest match on the resume. Owns enterprise accounts from implementation through ongoing value realization, runs QBRs/EBRs, manages account health and renewals - the exact arc of the Teladoc implementation-to-client-management progression.
watchOuts: Platform and data-connector configuration is more technical than Teladoc implementations. Lead with cross-functional delivery and stakeholder management rather than technical depth.

title: Senior Strategic Accounts Manager (Small Market)
why: Retention and upsell for small-group employer clients, advising on plan design and cost trends with broker relationships. Maps to the Plus One/Optum self-insured cost-containment work plus Teladoc enterprise client management.
watchOuts: Carries NRR and KPI targets - a commercial role, not pure service. Expect questions probing quota history.

title: Associate Principal, Partner Success (Care Partnerships)
why: Owns executive partner relationships, steering committees, and data-driven growth across health systems and clinics. The senior version of the Client Manager role, with the widest posted range here.
watchOuts: Health-system and clinic partnerships rather than employer or health-plan accounts - a real but crossable segment shift. Senior bar on executive presence.

title: Training & Content Operations Lead
why: The rare posting that rewards both halves of the resume: builds client-facing enablement material AND delivers live end-user and train-the-trainer sessions during implementations. Purdue Global teaching plus Teladoc implementation is an unusually clean fit.
watchOuts: Adobe Captivate and EMR/EHR exposure listed. Instructional-design tooling may need a quick self-directed ramp before interviews.

title: Strategic Client Relationship Manager - Payer, Optum Financial
why: Strategic payer account ownership: retention, renewals, upsell, executive relationships, value stories. She is an Optum alum through Plus One Health Management - a genuine warm-introduction angle.
watchOuts: Listing is tagged junior-level despite the senior range - clarify the actual band early. Up to 20% travel.

title: Manager, Client Success (Pharma)
why: Step up into people leadership - coaching a team of account managers while overseeing implementation, QBRs, and escalations. Teladoc mentoring and SME work is the evidence base for the management piece.
watchOuts: Pharma and agency clients, not employer benefits - the biggest industry jump here. Salesforce, Jira, and TaskRay listed as core tools.

title: Senior Client Success Manager (Strategic Accounts)
why: Subject-matter bullseye: maternity, fertility, and parenting benefits for large employer clients. Overlaps the Pomelo Care virtual maternity work and the lactation credential almost exactly.
watchOuts: No salary posted - confirm the band against the floor before investing. Verify the listing is still live; Maven runs several similar reqs at different levels.

title: Client Success Manager (Channel Partnerships)
why: Employer accounts arriving through channel partnerships, owning enrollment, engagement, and net revenue retention. Same domain advantage as the senior req, at a level that may convert faster.
watchOuts: Explicitly framed as commercial rather than service-oriented. No posted salary; likely below the senior band.

title: Client Success Manager
why: Retention, upsell, and NPS for strategic employer accounts, with a stated requirement for employer and payer benefits strategy knowledge - which the Teladoc and Optum years supply directly.
watchOuts: Geographic pay zones are the catch: a rural PA address likely lands in a lower zone, possibly under the floor. Ask which zone Susquehanna County falls in during the first screen.

title: Manager, Training and Enablement
why: Training program design and delivery for customer-facing teams - the adjunct teaching, webinar facilitation, and Teladoc SME work all point here.
watchOuts: Requires subject-matter depth in risk adjustment, medical economics, and contract forecasting. That gap is probably the deciding factor.

title: Founding Enterprise Customer Success Lead
why: Enterprise CS ownership from pilot through expansion, running executive cadence and building onboarding playbooks from scratch - suits someone repeatedly first-in with new clients.
watchOuts: Roughly 30% travel, and the product is AI voice agents and APIs. Founding-role ambiguity plus a technical product make this the biggest stretch that still clears the floor.

title: Director of Customer Success
why: Director-level health plan relationship ownership, business reviews, and product adoption. Highest-titled role here, and health-plan account management is squarely in her lane.
watchOuts: Posted as California-remote, which usually means CA residency required. Confirm they will hire an East Coast candidate first.
